promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.

learningObjectives.title: Enzyme action and the active site model
Effect of temperature on enzyme activity
Effect of pH on enzyme activity

questions.q: Which statement best defines a catalyst?
options: A substance that increases the rate of a reaction and is not changed by the reaction
A substance that is used up as a reaction proceeds
A substance that slows down the rate of a chemical reaction
A substance that supplies energy to start a reaction
questions.explain: A catalyst speeds up a reaction without itself being changed or used up, so it can be reused.

questions.q: Enzymes are biological catalysts made of which type of molecule?
options: Proteins
Carbohydrates
Lipids
Nucleic acids
questions.explain: Enzymes are proteins that function as biological catalysts inside living organisms.

questions.q: What happens to an enzyme molecule after it has catalysed a reaction?
options: It is unchanged and can be used again
It is permanently used up
It becomes part of the product
It is broken down into amino acids
questions.explain: Like all catalysts, an enzyme is not changed by the reaction, so a small amount can catalyse many reactions.

questions.q: What is the name of the region of an enzyme where the substrate binds?
options: The active site
The binding chain
The reaction pocket
The catalytic ring
questions.explain: The active site is the specific region of the enzyme with a shape complementary to its substrate.

questions.q: In enzyme reactions, the substance that an enzyme acts upon is called the:
options: Substrate
Product
Catalyst
Reagent
questions.explain: The substrate binds to the active site and is converted into the product(s).

questions.q: What is the approximate optimum temperature for most human enzymes?
questions.explain: Human enzymes work fastest at around 37 °C, close to normal body temperature.

questions.q: What term describes the permanent change to an enzyme's shape that stops it working at high temperature or extreme pH?
options: Denaturation
Digestion
Neutralisation
Respiration
questions.explain: Denaturation is the permanent change to the enzyme's structure, altering the active site so the substrate no longer fits.

questions.q: Why can a very small quantity of enzyme catalyse the conversion of a large amount of substrate?
options: The enzyme is not used up, so each molecule is used repeatedly
The enzyme grows as it works
The enzyme divides to make more enzyme
The enzyme becomes part of the product each time
questions.explain: Because enzymes are unchanged by the reactions they catalyse, each molecule can be reused many times.

questions.q: Why does a particular enzyme catalyse only one type of reaction?
options: Its active site has a shape complementary to only one substrate
It only works at one fixed temperature
It contains only one amino acid
It can only bind very large molecules
questions.explain: Enzymes are specific because only a substrate with a complementary shape fits into the active site.

questions.q: When a substrate binds to an enzyme, what is temporarily formed?
options: An enzyme-substrate complex
A permanent enzyme-product bond
A new enzyme molecule
A denatured active site
questions.explain: The substrate fits into the active site to form an enzyme-substrate complex before products are released.

questions.q: As temperature increases from 10 °C towards the optimum, why does enzyme activity increase?
options: Molecules move faster, so there are more successful collisions between enzyme and substrate
The active site changes shape to fit better
The enzyme is denatured, releasing energy
The substrate is destroyed more slowly
questions.explain: Higher temperature gives molecules more kinetic energy, increasing the frequency of enzyme-substrate collisions.

questions.q: Why does enzyme activity fall sharply above the optimum temperature?
options: The active site changes shape so the substrate no longer fits
The enzyme starts to reproduce rapidly
The substrate becomes too cold to react
The enzyme becomes a stronger catalyst
questions.explain: High temperature denatures the enzyme, altering the active site so the substrate can no longer bind.

questions.q: How does a pH far from an enzyme's optimum usually affect the enzyme?
options: It denatures the enzyme, changing the shape of the active site
It makes the enzyme catalyse the reaction faster
It turns the enzyme into a substrate
It has no effect on any enzyme
questions.explain: Extremes of pH denature the enzyme, altering the active site so the substrate no longer fits.

questions.q: Which statement about a denatured enzyme is correct?
options: Its active site has changed shape and it can no longer function
It works faster than before
It has simply been slowed down and will recover on cooling
It has been converted into its substrate
questions.explain: Denaturation permanently changes the active site's shape so the substrate can no longer bind.

questions.q: The enzyme pepsin works in the stomach. In which pH range does it work best?
options: A low (acidic) pH of about 2
A neutral pH of 7
A high (alkaline) pH of about 11
A pH of exactly 14
questions.explain: Pepsin has an acidic optimum pH of around 2, matching the acidic conditions of the stomach.

questions.q: In an experiment, an enzyme's reaction rate rises from 20 °C to a peak at 40 °C, then drops to zero by 60 °C. What best explains the drop after 40 °C?
options: The enzyme is being denatured as temperature rises above its optimum
The substrate has completely run out only above 40 °C
The enzyme is reproducing and using up the substrate
Collisions between molecules stop happening above 40 °C
questions.explain: Above the optimum of 40 °C the enzyme denatures, so its active site changes shape and activity falls to zero.

questions.q: A student tests an enzyme at pH 5, 7 and 9 and finds the fastest rate at pH 7 with much lower rates at 5 and 9. What can be concluded?
options: The optimum pH of this enzyme is about 7
The enzyme has no optimum pH
The enzyme works best in strong acid
pH has no effect on this enzyme
questions.explain: The highest activity occurs at pH 7, so that is the enzyme's optimum pH, with activity falling either side.

questions.q: An enzyme that breaks down starch will not break down protein. Which idea best explains this?
options: The protein does not have a shape complementary to the enzyme's active site
Protein molecules are too cold to react
The enzyme is used up by starch first
Protein cannot exist at the enzyme's optimum pH
questions.explain: Enzymes are specific, so only a substrate with a complementary shape (starch here) fits the active site.
